# write_setting { #crossrepo.config.write_setting }

```python
crossrepo.config.write_setting(text, key, value)
```

Put one setting into a configuration file, leaving the rest of it alone.

Only the lines the setting is written on are touched, so comments, key
order and spacing survive: a configuration file is written by hand and read
in diffs, and changing one setting should show up in one as that setting and
nothing else.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

<code>[**text**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Content of the file.

<code>[**key**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Setting to write.

<code>[**value**]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} []{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   Its new value.

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

<code>[]{.parameter-name} [:]{.parameter-annotation-sep} [[str](`str`)]{.parameter-annotation}</code>

:   The file with the setting written, appended at the end when it was not already there.
